response.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT z.city, COUNT(*) AS attendee_count FROM attendance AS a JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN zip_code AS z ON z.zip_code = m.zip GROUP BY z.city), city_shares AS (SELECT city, attendee_count, 1.0 * attendee_count / SUM(attendee_count) OVER () AS share FROM city_counts), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS average_city_share FROM city_shares) SELECT AVG(c.attendee_count) AS average_attendees, AVG(c.share) AS average_share, AVG(c.share - b.average_city_share) AS average_excess_share FROM city_shares AS c CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b WHERE c.share > b.average_city_share;

assumptions.assumption: Each attendance row counts as one attendee occurrence; a member attending multiple events is counted multiple times. Attendees without a matching ZIP code are excluded because their city cannot be determined.

alternatives.interpretation: Count each attending member once across all events.
alternatives.sql: WITH city_counts AS (SELECT z.city, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS attendee_count FROM attendance AS a JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN zip_code AS z ON z.zip_code = m.zip GROUP BY z.city), city_shares AS (SELECT city, attendee_count, 1.0 * attendee_count / SUM(attendee_count) OVER () AS share FROM city_counts), benchmark AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS average_city_share FROM city_shares) SELECT AVG(c.attendee_count) AS average_attendees, AVG(c.share) AS average_share, AVG(c.share - b.average_city_share) AS average_excess_share FROM city_shares AS c CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b WHERE c.share > b.average_city_share;
